hero.subtitle: Whether you were injured at a warehouse near Valley View Street or on a job site off Ball Road, Cypress workers face real questions about who pays for a workplace injury. We can help you understand workers' comp and explore what other options may be available to you at no cost.

about.title: Cypress Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Cypress sits in a busy stretch of Orange County where warehouses, retail centers, and light industrial sites line corridors like Walker Street and Lincoln Avenue. When someone gets hurt on the job here, the first assumption is usually workers' compensation — and in most cases, that's correct, since California treats it as the exclusive remedy against an employer regardless of fault. But workplace injuries aren't always that simple. If a subcontractor, equipment manufacturer, property owner, or another driver contributed to what happened, a separate claim against that third party may be possible alongside any workers' comp benefits. Sorting out which path applies, and whether more than one applies, is where our review matters. We handle injured workers' claims directly — we look at the details and explain what options actually exist.

items.title: Understanding the 30-Day Reporting Window
items.desc: California requires an injured worker to report the incident to their employer within 30 days to preserve workers' comp rights. We can help make sure that step, and any follow-up paperwork, doesn't get missed or mishandled.

items.title: Spotting a Third-Party Claim
items.desc: Workers' comp is usually the only remedy against an employer, but if a subcontractor, property owner, or equipment maker played a role, a separate injury claim may be available. We can review the facts and determine whether that door is open.

items.title: Protection Against Retaliation
items.desc: California law makes it illegal for an employer to retaliate against a worker for reporting an injury or filing a claim. If you feel pressured or penalized, we can address that as part of the bigger picture.

items.question: If I already filed a workers' comp claim in Cypress, can I still talk to an attorney about a third-party claim?
items.answer: Yes. Workers' comp and a third-party claim aren't mutually exclusive — they run on different tracks. If someone other than your employer, like a subcontractor or equipment manufacturer, contributed to your injury, a separate claim against them may still be possible. A third-party claim carries its own two-year deadline, so it's worth having it reviewed sooner rather than later.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a claim against a third party after a workplace injury in Cypress?
items.answer: California generally gives injured workers two years from the date of injury to file a third-party injury claim. This is separate from the workers' comp reporting deadline. Missing that window can close off options, so getting a claim reviewed early is generally a good idea.

items.question: My employer near Ball Road told me not to file a claim — is that allowed?
items.answer: No. California law prohibits employers from retaliating against workers for reporting an injury or pursuing a workers' comp claim. If that's happening, we can explain your rights and next steps at no cost.
